findings.title: Unescaped remote JSON values written into HTML response (XSS)
findings.explanation: The resource is declared @Produces("text/html") and streams a hand-built HTML document to the browser. Values taken straight out of the parsed JSON feed (farm, server, id, secret) are concatenated into an tag at line 74 with no HTML or attribute encoding and no validation that they are numeric/hex. Any of these JSON string values may contain '"', '>', or '<', so a value such as "\">" breaks out of the attribute and the tag and executes script in the origin that serves /parser. The feed data is not trustworthy from the servlet's point of view: it is fetched at line 53 over cleartext http:// (http://api.flickr.com/...), so any network-position attacker (or a DNS/proxy hijack, or malicious/compromised content served by the upstream API) fully controls the JSON body and therefore the HTML emitted to every user who requests this endpoint. The parser itself performs no escaping - JsonParser.getString() returns the raw decoded string - so no sanitization happens anywhere on the path.
